slots.hypothesis: Core A is the log ratio of last-hour to first-hour geometric-mean minute volume. It does not change when the day's volume is multiplied by a constant, so it cannot be a proxy for turnover or size. On its own it scores +0.547. Its 20-day mean is the top head at +1.668 (valid 2.26). Round-1 R showed the log form is the only normalization that works. It is not on the mechanical core cards. The family control holds 1 head (round 1's E failed with 5), and the only periphery seen is {cross_mean}. There are no smoothing seeds, because the library rank ban (>= 0.7) would reject them. The 15 seeds cover three kinds of periphery. (1) Time structure of the core: 20-day std, 60-day robust z, 5-day vs 60-day drift, 20-day vs 240-day deviation, and upper or lower tail mean minus mean. (2) Noise standardization: mean/std across days and within the day. (3) Second-leaf decompositions and interactions: Amt curve minus Volume curve (price drift between first and last hour), Volume curve minus High-Low curve, 60-day correlation of the core with daily return and with log daily volume, 60-day beta to the market-wide core, a conditional sort by price drift, and the core times gini.

This applies extreme-value time aggregation (soft-max or MAX) as a general treatment. It comes from M2's dose-response on pow_2(pow_2_5(day_durbin_watson(High))). Exponents 1, 2, 2.5 and 5 score -1.17, +0.27, +0.72 and +1.45, with the same daily cross-section, because EMA runs on raw values before z-rank. It also follows the MAX effect of Bali, Cakici and Whitelaw (2011). The inputs avoid realized-variance levels, which the DW(High) rank ban would reject: volume gini, DW(Volume), max-minute volume share, max and min minute return, intraday skew and kurtosis, signed buying pressure, zero-return share, at-max-ratio of Close (limit locks), flat_run_max(Vwap), and the return of the heaviest minutes. The 16 seeds use four forms: a convex power fed straight into EMA (the same form as the head), a convex power then a 20-day mean, an explicit cross_max or cross_tail_mean_q75/q25, and the tail divided by the mean.
